chapter: Television, vocal albums and orchestral craft
title: Bass saxophone and baritone setups
summary: They compare Clare Fischer's sax section with bass saxophone and Kenton's two baritones, with Mandel saying the top baritone gets the part nobody wants.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Have you heard the things Clare Fischer did for six saxes with two altos, two tenors, baritone and a bass on the bottom?
No, I haven't but I don't think that's a very good combination because the baritone will have a dumb part.
He’s sitting up on the upper part of his horn and it's not a real good sound, in the section because the good notes are going to the bass saxophone, which is a relatively clumsy instrument.

It’s a good instrument it’s just, I used to use it a lot more than I do now, I like bass saxophone. But I’d use it in place of baritone if I just wanted to extend the range rather than having a baritone up above it. I never liked the Kenton two baritone set up either.
‘Cause the top baritone’s got the part nobody wants.
The bottom baritone has the best part in the band.
